new possibilities for video generation, with potential appli-

Recent text-to-video generation models [3, 11, 16, 26,
27, 44] have demonstrated promising results by leverag-
ing large-scale video datasets [10, 28, 46]. Despite these
advances, existing datasets present limitations that affect
model training effectiveness. These datasets face two pri-
mary challenges: 1) video quality issues, including tem-
poral inconsistencies from imprecise scene detection and
prevalence of static content lacking motion dynamics; 2)
caption quality limitations, manifested in frame-by-frame
descriptions rather than coherent narratives, insufficient de-
scriptive details with limited word counts, and inadequate
semantic alignment between text and video content.
To
address these challenges, we introduce CFC-VIDS-1M,
constructed through a systematic coarse-to-fine curation
pipeline that ensures both visual and caption quality.
Our proposed coarse-to-fine curation pipeline addresses
dataset quality through two systematic stages.
At the
coarse level, we evaluate video quality across multiple di-
mensions including aesthetic appeal, temporal consistency,
OCR presence, motion dynamics, and category distribution.
Each dimension is quantitatively assessed using specialized
models. The fine-grained stage focuses on enhancing text-
video alignment through a two-step process that leverages
vision-language and large language models, ensuring both
caption informativeness and semantic accuracy.
To fully leverage the curated CFC-VIDS-1M dataset
for text-to-video synthesis, efficient architectures and train-
ing strategies are crucial. We develop a transformer-based
model RACCOON with decoupled spatial-temporal atten-
tion mechanisms, enabling efficient processing of video
sequences.
Building upon this architecture, we propose
a four-stage training strategy that progressively enhances
model capabilities: beginning with semantic learning from
pre-trained image models, followed by temporal model-
ing at low resolution, then scaling to high-resolution video
generation, and finally refining visual quality through tar-
geted fine-tuning. This systematic approach effectively ad-
dresses the computational challenges of video generation
while maintaining generation quality.

**Answer:**

**1. Core Innovation:**  
The research introduces a comprehensive approach combining advanced data curation and transformer-based diffusion models for text-to-video generation. It features a systematic coarse-to-fine curation pipeline ensuring high visual and caption quality, and a four-stage training strategy for efficient and effective video generation.

**2. Technical Approach:**  
- **Curation Pipeline:** Uses multi-dimensional quality assessments (video quality, OCR, temporal consistency, category, motion) and model-based caption enhancement.  
- **Transformer Model:** RACCOON employs decoupled spatial-temporal attention mechanisms for efficient processing.  
- **Training Strategy:** A four-stage approach including semantic learning, temporal modeling, high-resolution generation, and targeted fine-tuning.

**3. Quantitative Findings:**  
- **Dataset:** CFC-VIDS-1M achieves 89.3 words per frame with 10.6 seconds average duration.  
- **Performance Metrics:** Improved temporal consistency (TC) and visual quality metrics (Aes, Motion) compared to baseline datasets.  
- **Sample Size:** The model processes 70 million text-video pairs, demonstrating scalability and efficiency.

**4. Limitations & Assumptions:**  
- Assumes sufficient labeling quality for curation.  
- Relies on pre-trained vision models for semantic understanding.  
- Focuses on single-domain video generation, limiting multi-domain applicability.

**5. Domain Impact:**  
- **Theoretical:** Advances diffusion models for video synthesis with improved efficiency and quality.  
- **Practical:** Enables applications in creative content, education, and visual storytelling, enhancing user experience through high-quality, temporally coherent outputs.
